title: 6 months of solo part-time dev on my first game: a medieval open-world RPG in Godot (teaser)
author: DometGames
selftext:
Hi everyone!



This is The Last Eagle, the first game I've ever made. I've been working on it for about 6 months, part time, mostly alone (my girlfriend helps me from time to time – she's the reason some parts look as good as they do ❤️).



Why I'm making it:

Honestly, I'm making the game I want to play myself. I've played pretty much every medieval game out there and they all inspired me in some way. I wanted one big world where everything feels like it belongs to that era.



What it's aiming for:

\- A medieval setting where everything you use, wear and build belongs to that era

\- 9 continents: Ravenia, Visara, Aurelia, Khemara, Skarn, Qirin, Ilvaros, Tashkar and Norvane

\- You can zoom out and see the whole planet, then sail and travel to other continents

\- Walk into villages, castles and cities. Trade, talk to people, take on tasks

\- Build and lead your own army

\- Arena fights, sieges and field battles



The Godot side:

\- Godot 4 + Terrain3D for the world map

\- The planet view, curved horizon and travelling between continents were the hardest parts so far

\- Characters run on an AnimationTree setup with retargeted animations, plus spring bones for capes and clothes

\- Happy to answer questions about any of it!



Being transparent:

\- Characters, buildings, most props and all sounds are bought asset packs, which I build and modify on top of

\- Some 3D props and UI art (title screen, icons) were generated with Meshy AI, then edited by me

\- I use an AI coding assistant (Claude) to help write and debug code

\- The teaser was captured in-game and edited by me



My setup:

Everything you see was made and recorded on a pretty modest PC – Ryzen 5 3600, RX 580 and 16 GB RAM. Optimizing for older hardware is a big part of my work.



Everything in the teaser is work in progress and will change. My goal is for this to look genuinely good one day, and to eventually turn this part-time project into my main job.



I'd really love to hear what you think – what looks good, what looks off, and what you'd want from a game like this.



Thanks for watching! 🦅



YouTube (just getting started): [https://www.youtube.com/@dometgames1](https://www.youtube.com/@dometgames1)

comments.author: Jameshardy1988
comments.body:
Wow congrats this looks awesome, make sure you do another post once you add it to steam (Assuming here) as id definitely wishlist it.

How did you manage to get the combat so polished? I've struggled to get it much better than hitting the air in front of their opponents

replies.author: DometGames
replies.body:
Thank you so much! Definitely, I'll post something new in the next few days, and I hope to get it on Steam soon.

Honestly, combat was hell. Same problem as you at first, swords hitting air. What fixed it for me:

\- Hit detection along the actual blade, a hit only counts when the edge enters the opponent's body

\- Directional swings and blocks from mouse movement

\- Swing commit + rebound when blades clash, so it doesn't feel floaty

\- Finishers, hand-keyed in Blender, which made a huge difference to how it feels

Still lots to polish. If I manage to raise enough funding, I'm open to buying better combat animations and upgrading what I've built so far. The final goal is to get motion capture gear and make my own animations.

comments.author: Klov1233
comments.body: Bro i use Claude Code with Vs code with Mcp Unity and sometimes Mcp blender but i dont know how should i create assets map and stuff with ai

replies.author: DometGames
replies.body:
Hey! Here are a few things that helped me:

\- Learn some Blender basics first. Blender Guru's "Donut" tutorial on YouTube is a great place to start.

\- Use existing asset packs as a starting point. You can find free and paid assets on Fab and similar stores, then modify them to fit your game. It's often much faster than creating everything from scratch.

\- Try Meshy AI for smaller props and Poly Haven for free textures and skyboxes.

\- For maps, I use Godot with the Terrain3D plugin, so I'm not sure how it works in Unity, but Unity has its own Terrain tools with plenty of tutorials on YouTube. 

My biggest advice is to start small, experiment with different tools, and build on what works rather than trying to create everything from scratch right away.

comments.author: Dizz-ie10
comments.body: Did you make the map with ai or do you have modelling experience?

replies.author: DometGames
replies.body: A mix of both! The base shape of the continents was generated with Python scripts (with AI helping me write them), and then the terrain was hand-sculpted in Terrain3D (a free terrain plugin for Godot), a big part of that by my girlfriend. No real modelling background, just a lot of learning as I go.

comments.author: SweetKarmaz
comments.body: This is amazing -  will there be magic or fantastical elements, or are you going more for realism? Are there going to be quests, or is it more a 'live the life' style where things are supposed to happen organically? And what is your plan for distribution?

replies.author: DometGames
replies.body:
Thank you! Going for realism, no magic. There will be quests from NPCs, but it's also very much a "live the life" style where things happen on their own in the world.

The plan: sandbox first, then co-op, and a full campaign at the end. PC is the first target, but long term I'd love it to be cross-platform, including PlayStation and even mobile

replies.author: SweetKarmaz
replies.body: One of the games I am making, and the furthest along, is a medieval settlement/survival game in a randomized voxel world. I heavily debated about adding magic and other things, but decided against it. I didn't want the first game I make to be longer and I am already 7 or 8 months into this one. I am making that in Unity - but the next two games are going to be in my own claude created custom editor that is 100% controllable in every way shape and form by claude (but also 100% controllable from the editor by a person!). One will be a single player RPG and the other is going to be another survival game but modern day.

replies.author: DometGames
replies.body: Oh nice, that sounds like something I'd actually play! Your custom editor sounds wild, would love to see it when it's ready. Good luck man!

replies.author: SweetKarmaz
replies.body: Once its actually being used, I will post about it, and make it available for others if they want to try it out.

replies.author: DometGames
replies.body: Awesome, I'll keep an eye out for it!
